text: Xin cho hỏi tên gì ạ?
ipa: sin˧ tʃɔ˧ hɔj˧˩˧ t̪en˧ zi˨˩ aː˨˩ˀ

text: Đây là con gái / con trai tôi
ipa: ɗəɪ˧ laː˨˩ kɔn˧ ɣaːj˧˥ / kɔn˧ tʃaːj˧ t̪oj˧

text: Tôi đi du lịch một mình
ipa: t̪oj˧ ɗi˧ zu˧ lic˨˩ˀ mot̪˨˩ˀ miɲ˨˩

literal: sinh viên (university/college student) rather than học sinh, which specifically means a K-12 pupil in Vietnamese

text: Tôi làm việc ở văn phòng
ipa: t̪oj˧ laːm˨˩ viɛ̯c˨˩ˀ əː˧˩˧ van˧ fɔŋ˨˩

literal: mẹ, the dictionary-standard word (má/mạ are regional)
cha, the dictionary-standard, pan-regional word (bố/ba are regional)

Vietnamese has no age-neutral word for brother -- anh trai (older) is the default English-Vietnamese dictionary gloss for the bare word (translate.com, vndic), against em trai (younger); a traveler with a younger brother needs em trai instead
chị gái (older), the parallel choice to this-is-my-brother's anh trai; a traveler with a younger sister needs em gái instead
người yêu (lit. person [I] love) is gender-neutral and not a business partner (đối tác)
